claim:
Let \(X=(\mathbb R^2,N)\), where
\[
N(s,t)=\max\{|s|,|t|,|s-t|\}.
\]
Then the ordinary Dunkl--Williams constant is
\[
DW(X)=\frac94.
\]
More precisely, in the two-dimensional frame formula \(DW(X)=2\max_{v\in\operatorname{ext}(B_X)}M(v)\), every extreme point satisfies
\[
M(v)=\frac98.
\]
At the representative vertex \(v=(1,1)\), a nonzero Birkhoff--James direction can, after scaling and swapping coordinates, be written as \(w=(q,-1)\) with \(q\ge1\), and its frame contribution is exactly
\[
m(v,w)=1+\frac{q-1}{2q^2}.
\]
Hence the unique maximizing direction ratio is \(q=2\), up to the hexagon's linear isometries and rescaling. The original Dunkl--Williams quotient is attained, for example, by
\[
x=(-1,-2),\qquad y=(-1,0).
\]
integrity: The exact value is derived from the verified two-dimensional frame theorem and a complete piecewise-linear calculation of every Birkhoff--James direction at a representative vertex. An explicit pair independently attains the final value in the original definition.
scientific_limitations: The result is for one real affine-regular hexagonal plane. It classifies the maximizing frame direction at every extreme point but does not claim a complete classification of all ordered pairs maximizing the original Dunkl--Williams quotient. The 2012 symmetric-octagonal article was not inspected in full.
title: Exact Dunkl--Williams constant of the affine-regular hexagonal plane
